full_judgment:
Md Abdul Aziz J: Criminal Appeal No. 172 of 1985 preferred by convict Mostafa alias Mostafizur Rahman and Criminal Appeal No. 216 of 1986 preferred by convict Abdus Shahid are directed against the same impugned judgment and order of conviction dated 29-2-1984 passed by the Special Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka in Special Tribunal Case No. 168 of 1977 convicting both the appellants under section 394 of the Penal Code and sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 5(five) years and to pay a fine of Taka 10,000 each, in default to suffer RI for a further period of 1(one) year. 

 2. The short prosecution case is, inter alia, that, on 16-11-1976 in the night PW 1 Montajuddin was called from his sleep at 12-30 by his cousin Safaruddin on the plea that some police personnel came and asked to open the door, whereupon PW 1 opened the door and immediately 3/4 persons entered his room and beating him and his wife committed dacoity by looting away cash and valuables worth about Taka 4,407 and PW 1 identified both the accused-appellants from the light of the burning lamp kept inside the room. 

 4. Prosecution examined five PWs in the case. The Special Tribunal convicted the appellants as aforesaid on consideration of the evidence of the PWs by its impugned judgment dated 29-2-1984 giving effect of the impugned judgment from the date of arrest of the appellants. 

 5. Both the appellants were released on bail in the case before trial but they did not turn up to face the trial. It appears from the memo of appeal of Criminal Appeal No. 172/1985 that after passing the impugned judgment on 29-2-84 appellant Mostafa alias Mostafizur Rahman of Criminal Appeal No. 172 of 1985 was arrested on 20-6-1985 by police. Thereafter, he filed the appeal on 12-8-85 under section 30 of the Special Powers Act, 1974. The appeal was thus out of time by 527 days. It appears from the memo of appeal of Criminal Appeal No. 216/1986 that convict-appellant Abdus Shahid of Criminal Appeal No. 216 of 1986 convicted and sentenced by the same judgment dated 29-2-84 was arrested on 25-6-85 and he filed the appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act, 1974 before this Division on 6-8-86. Thus, the appeal was out of time by 857 days. 

 9. At the time of hearing of the case the learned Advocate for the appellants was confronted with the question of legality and propriety of admitting the appeal filed under section 30 of the Special Powers Act, 1974 on condonation of delay under section 5 of the Limitation Act before going into the merit of the appeals. Mr Sk Afzalur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants finding himself in difficult position to address the point confronted with, submitted that for the ends of justice he prays for conversion of the Memo of Appeal into an application under section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and to dispose of the matters accordingly. In support of his submission Mr Rahman has referred a decision in the case between Sohail Ahmed Chowdhury vs State, reported in 47 DLR 482. 

 10. We have perused the impugned judgment and memo of appeals of both the appeals before us and also gone through the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the appellants. It appears from the reported judgment of the cited case that, having been convicted under section 25B(1) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life with a fine of Taka 5,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 year more the appellant Sohail Ahmed Chowdhury filed Criminal Appeal No. 713 of 1990 before the High Court Division and the same being time barred an application was filed for admission of the appeal after condoning the delay and a Rule (Criminal Revision 770(R)90 was issued by the Court on 3-9-90 which was heard by a Division Bench of this Court but before its disposal by the said Court the matter was sent to the subsequent Bench by the Hon'ble Chief Justice for hearing and disposal. 

 11. It appears from the judgment that as there was no scope for getting relief on the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act in respect of a time barred appeal arising out of conviction and sentence passed under the Special Powers Act, instead of pressing the application for condonation of delay for admission of the appeal, prayer was made on behalf of the accused-petitioner for conversion of the Criminal Appeal No. 713/90 along with Criminal Revision No. 770(R)/90 to an application for quashment of the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence invoking the aid of section 561-A of the CrPC and the said prayer was allowed after hearing and the Memo of Appeal was converted into an application under section 561-A of the CrPC and registered as Criminal Misc. Case No. 944 of 1995 calling in question the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence. 

 12. It appears from perusal of the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the appellants as aforesaid that, before hearing or for that matter, before pressing the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act in the time barred Criminal Appeal No. 713/1990 for admitting the appeal on condonation of delay finding that there was no scope for getting any relief on the said application, the learned Advocate for the appeIlant prayed for conversion of the said Criminal Appeal to an application for quashment of the impugned judgment invoking the aid of section 561 A of the Cr PC and the same was all owed on hearing both the sides. But in the cases before us there is no such scope for converting the Criminal Appeal Nos. 172/1985 and 216/1986 to an application for quashment of the impugned judgment and order of conviction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as both the appeals have already been admitted after condonation of delay vide order dated 3-9-85 by a Single Bench of this Division and, as such, no appeal nor for that matter, any application under section 5 of the Limitation Act is pending for admission before us for disposal. We, therefore, are of the opinion that the aforesaid decision has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the cases before us. 

 17. The impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed against the convict-appellants in both the appeals in Special Tribunal Case No. 168/1977 by the Special Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka are hereby maintained.
